title: Dualizing complexes over essentially finite type complete-local bases
statement: Let $(C,\mathfrak n)$ be a commutative Noetherian complete local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $A$ be a commutative $C$-algebra which is a localization of a finitely generated $C$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Then $A$ has an algebraic dualizing complex in the sense of [def-per-algebraic-normalized-dualizing].

proof.text: By the localization hypothesis choose a finite type $C$-algebra $B$ and a multiplicative subset $S\subseteq B$ with $A=S^{-1}B$. By [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], choose $n\ge0$ and a surjection $P=C[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow B$. The case $n=0$ means $P=C$. We will construct a dualizing complex first for $C$, next for $P$ and $B$, and finally localize to $A$.

The given completeness is completeness for the maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cohen-power-series-presentation] to $(C,\mathfrak n)$. It gives a surjective local homomorphism $q:R\twoheadrightarrow C$ with $R$ a complete Noetherian regular local ring. Apply [lem-trf-regular-local-bounded-injective-resolution] to $R$: there is a bounded complex $I^\bullet$ of injective $R$-modules representing $R[0]$.

source.place: Tag 0BFR, lemma-ubiquity-dualizing, proof of (2), invoking algebra.tex Tag 032A and dualizing.tex Tag 0AWX.

proof.text: We verify the other two dualizing conditions on $R[0]$. Its only nonzero cohomology is the cyclic module $R$ in degree zero. The bounded injective complex $I^\bullet$ of Step 2 is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective], so [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] computes $R\operatorname{Hom}_R(R[0],R[0])$ by $\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(R[0],I^\bullet)$. Evaluation $f\mapsto f(1)$ identifies this complex with $I^\bullet$; its inverse in degree $j$ sends $v\in I^j$ to $[r\mapsto rv]$, and both maps commute with the differentials. Under this identification the scalar-action map is the chosen quasi-isomorphism $R[0]\to I^\bullet$. It is therefore an isomorphism in $D(R)$. Together with Step 2 these are exactly the three conditions of [def-per-algebraic-normalized-dualizing]. Thus $R[0]$ is algebraically dualizing.

source.place: Tag 0AWX, lemma-regular-gorenstein, proof: verification that R[0] is dualizing from finite self-injective dimension.

proof.text: The quotient $C$ is a finite $R$-module, generated by $1$: every $c\in C$ is $q(r)1$ for a lift $r\in R$. Both $R$ and $C$ are Noetherian. Apply [lem-trf-finite-map-dualizing-transfer] to $q$ and $L=R[0]$, with the three properties just verified. It gives $\Omega_C=R\operatorname{Hom}_R(C,R[0])$, with its specified $C$-action, having finite $C$-cohomology, a bounded injective $C$-representative, and an invertible scalar-action map. By [def-per-algebraic-normalized-dualizing], $\Omega_C$ is an algebraic dualizing complex for $C$. Choose a complex $K_0^\bullet$ representing it.

source.place: Tag 0BFR (2), using Tag 0AX0, lemma-dualizing-finite (the surjective case of lemma-dualizing-quotient).

proof.text: Put $P_j=C[x_1,\ldots,x_j]$, for $0\le j\le n$. Each $P_j$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], since it is generated by its $j$ variables over the Noetherian ring $C$. Define successively $K_j^\bullet=K_{j-1}^\bullet\otimes_{P_{j-1}}P_{j-1}[x_j]$ termwise. Induct on $j$: for $j=0$, Step 4 gives the dualizing property over $P_0=C$; if $K_{j-1}^\bullet$ is dualizing over $P_{j-1}$, [lem-per-algebraic-dualizing-polynomial] applies to this Noetherian ring and that complex and proves $K_j^\bullet$ dualizing over $P_j$. At $j=n$ this gives an algebraic dualizing complex $\Omega_P$ over $P$. For $n=0$ the induction takes no steps.

source.place: Tag 0BFR (5); proposition-dualizing-essentially-finite-type, polynomial operation Tag 0A7J, lemma-dualizing-polynomial-ring, iterated finitely many times.

proof.text: The finite type $C$-algebra $B$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. The surjection $P\twoheadrightarrow B$ makes $B$ a finite $P$-module generated by $1$, and Step 5 gives the Noetherian hypothesis on $P$. Apply [lem-trf-finite-map-dualizing-transfer] to this map and $\Omega_P$. Its hypotheses on the complex are exactly the three conditions of [def-per-algebraic-normalized-dualizing]. Thus $\Omega_B=R\operatorname{Hom}_P(B,\Omega_P)$ has all three dualizing properties over $B$, with the action specified by the transfer theorem. Choose a representative $K_B^\bullet$. This applies also to $B=0$, whose zero complex satisfies the conditions.

source.place: Tag 0BFR (5); proposition-dualizing-essentially-finite-type, quotient operation Tag 0A7I, lemma-dualizing-quotient, a special case of Tag 0AX0.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-algebraic-dualizing-localization] to the Noetherian ring $B$, the multiplicative subset $S$ and $K_B^\bullet$. It gives an algebraic dualizing complex represented by $S^{-1}K_B^\bullet$ over $A=S^{-1}B$, as required. For completeness, $A$ is Noetherian directly: an ideal $J\subseteq S^{-1}B$ is generated by the images of generators of its contraction to $B$, since $b/s\in J$ implies $b/1=(s/1)(b/s)\in J$ and conversely $b/s=(1/s)(b/1)$. The contraction is finitely generated by Noetherianity of $B$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. No normalization at local rings is requested by the item; the conclusion is the global algebraic-dualizing predicate.
